disclosed_facts.fact: Company describes itself as a vertically integrated owner, developer and operator of large-scale digital infrastructure purpose-built for HPC/AI workloads, controlling land through ownership or long-term ground leases together with interconnection rights, electrical and cooling infrastructure and, where applicable, on-site generation, delivering capacity to hyperscale and enterprise customers under long-term hosting arrangements.
Contracted HPC platform across two primary campuses (Lake Mariner, Barker NY in NYISO; Abernathy, TX in SPP) totaling 522 MW of contracted critical IT load with long-dated revenue visibility.

December 2024: subsidiary La Lupa entered long-term data center lease agreements with Core42 committing to deliver 60 MW of critical IT load; initial ten-year term with two five-year renewal options, plus operating standards, service levels and expansion rights; commissioning commenced 2025 with phased deliveries.

August 2025: subsidiary Akela entered three data center leases with Fluidstack USA I Inc. (described as a leading AI cloud platform) to provide 378 MW of critical IT load at Lake Mariner; construction commenced 2025, delivery expected to commence 2026; leases benefit from substantial credit support from Google backing Fluidstack's payment and performance obligations.

Abernathy HPC Campus designed for 168 MW critical IT load (full site build-out) fully pre-leased to Fluidstack USA III under a 25-year data center lease with built-in rent escalators and term-contraction options, with Google credit support; developed through a joint venture (FS CS 1 LLC) in which the Company holds a 50.1% interest under an amended and restated LLC agreement with Fluidstack CS I Inc.; delivery targeted 2H 2026.

Lake Mariner is on the site of a retired coal-fired power plant with substantial existing transmission infrastructure; as of Dec 31, 2025 it operated 245 MW of legacy bitcoin mining capacity and 18 MW of critical IT HPC capacity, with phased expansion to ~500 MW gross near term and potential ~750 MW subject to additional NYISO approvals; 90 MW is allocated under a February 2022 NYPA agreement providing high-load-factor power over a ten-year term from initial delivery.

Long-term ground lease at the Cayuga Site (Lansing, NY) with existing interconnection and supporting infrastructure, which upon permitting and site development could support up to 400 MW gross / ~320 MW contractual critical IT load as a third anchor location in the development pipeline.
Stated development model targets contracting approximately 250 MW to 500 MW of new critical IT HPC capacity annually, aligned with customer demand and power availability.

Company states it has deliberately transitioned toward HPC hosting as its primary business and that capital allocation will focus on HPC data center development and AI-compute infrastructure, while it currently derives the majority of revenue from bitcoin mining.

HPC lease revenue of $31.9 million for the three months and $53.0 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 (vs. none in the prior-year periods), out of total revenue of $44.8 million and $78.8 million respectively; digital asset revenue was $12.8 million and $25.8 million.

Property, plant and equipment, net rose to $3.60 billion at June 30, 2026 from $1.51 billion at December 31, 2025, with accrued construction liabilities of $287.5 million, reflecting ongoing data center build-out.

July 6, 2026: subsidiary Raylan Data LLC entered a 20-year lease with Anthropic PBC as tenant to provide approximately 401 MW of critical IT load for HPC at the Justified Data Campus in Hawesville, Kentucky; rent commences upon delivery of each leased premises (phased delivery beginning late 2027, concluding early 2028), with two five-year renewal options; Anthropic's payment obligations expected to be supported by an investment-grade credit.

July 6, 2026: subsidiary Big Country Wulf LLC entered a Membership Interest Purchase Agreement with Fluidstack CS I Inc. and other purchasers relating to the Abernathy joint venture interests (Abernathy Transaction), closed on the Closing Date.

May 2026: entered a MIPA with Industrial Equity Partners to acquire the Muskie Data Campus in Eastern Kentucky — approximately 285 acres of owned and controlled land, with an option on adjacent acreage, expected to support up to 1 GW of data center capacity (initial 500 MW ramping from 2H 2028, additional 500 MW targeted 2H 2030); acquisition closed without third-party consents or regulatory approvals.

At Muskie, Kentucky Power (an AEP company) is constructing a 345 kV substation connected to the existing 765 kV transmission network to support the full 1+ GW campus; transmission infrastructure and energy service agreements were executed concurrently with the MIPA under the applicable Industrial General Service large-load tariff.

April 2026 underwritten equity offering of 47,400,000 shares at $19.00 (plus a 30-day option on 7,110,000 additional shares) generating approximately $1,004.3 million of net proceeds, closed April 16, 2026.

Stated competitive strength: originates and controls large contiguous sites with access to cost-competitive power and 'the interconnection rights necessary to energize high-density compute at scale'; management states securing power and interconnection ahead of demand is the principal constraint on new HPC capacity.

As of May 31, 2026, executed long-term leases representing approximately 1,410 MW of contracted critical IT load across five campuses, approximately $36.2 billion of total contracted revenue over initial 15-year base terms; each lease is direct with CoreWeave or an investment-grade hyperscaler, structured take-or-pay and non-cancellable, with termination for convenience requiring payment of full remaining contractual value.

Polaris Forge 1 (Ellendale, ND): ELN-02 and ELN-03 data center leases signed May 28, 2025 with CoreWeave, Inc. for an aggregate 250 MW, plus an August 28, 2025 Building 4 Lease with CoreWeave for an additional 150 MW, bringing total contracted capacity with CoreWeave at that campus to 400 MW (~$11.0B contracted revenue over 15 years); Company guaranteed the subsidiaries' obligations.

On March 30, 2026, following CoreWeave internal restructuring, the ELN-02 Lease was amended and the ELN-03 Lease assigned to CoreWeave Compute Acquisition Co. VIII, LLC, a wholly owned CoreWeave subsidiary.

Polaris Forge 2 (Harwood, ND): approximately 15-year lease entered October 22, 2025 with a U.S.-based investment-grade hyperscaler for 200 MW of critical IT load (~$5.0B contracted revenue; two five-year renewal options).

Delta Forge 1 (southern U.S. market, 300 MW): two approximately 15-year leases entered April 23, 2026 with a second U.S.-based investment-grade hyperscaler for an aggregate 300 MW of critical IT load (~$7.5B contracted revenue).

Polaris Forge 3: 300 MW critical IT load under two ~15-year leases (with three five-year renewal options) with a high investment-grade hyperscaler, representing approximately $7.5 billion of contracted revenue over the base term, delivery 2H27–2H28.

Delta Forge 2: full 210 MW of critical IT load contracted under an ~15-year lease (three five-year renewal options) with a high investment-grade hyperscaler, approximately $5.2 billion of contracted revenue over the base term, expected delivery 1H28.

First HPC data center at Polaris Forge 1 with approximately 100 MW of critical IT load became operational in October 2025; a second 150 MW building is partially operational and a third ~150 MW building is under construction (RFS calendar 2027).

As of May 31, 2026, approximately 1.5 GW of critical IT load contracted and operating or under construction across five campuses, of which approximately 100 MW was operating and revenue-generating; each MW backed by land under Company control and/or an executed utility power agreement.

Active development pipeline of over 3 GW of utility (gross) power and an extended pipeline of more than 5 GW in earlier-stage discussion/due diligence; certain greenfield sites scalable to 1 GW or more.

Partnership with Base Electron Corporation, an independent power producer, pursuing development of approximately 1.2 GW of front-of-the-meter natural gas-fired generation in the Dakotas to unlock additional power capacity for the development pipeline.

Company holds master service and master telecom service agreements with leading hyperscalers, described as difficult to obtain, and its standardized design has been qualified by major hyperscalers; campuses engineered for liquid-cooled high-density GPU deployments (~150 MW delivered in ~14–18 months).
